LESSON: GUIDED WRITING: PARAGRAPH WRITING

Grade: Grade 6
Subject: ARABIC LANGUAGE
Strand: Writing 3.7 Guided Writing: Sentences (2 sessions) • Vocabulary- Grooming practi
Topic 3.9: Guided Writing: Paragraph Writing
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Guided Writing: Paragraph Writing, part of Writing 3.7 Guided Writing: Sentences (2 sessions) • Vocabulary- Grooming practi in Grade 6 ARABIC LANGUAGE.

Key inquiry question: How do we take care of our school facilities? 2. How do we form paragraph?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

A. identify features of well- developed paragraph,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Guided Writing: Paragraph Writing in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

B. compose a paragraph using acquired vocabulary for effective communication,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Guided Writing: Paragraph Writing in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

C. develop positive attitude towards writing in Arabic for enjoyment.

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Guided Writing: Paragraph Writing in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. identify features of well- developed paragraph,

   Guided Writing: Paragraph Writing helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

B. compose a paragraph using acquired vocabulary for effective communication,

   Guided Writing: Paragraph Writing helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

C. develop positive attitude towards writing in Arabic for enjoyment.

   Guided Writing: Paragraph Writing helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

D. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. collaborate to conduct a research on the features of a well- developed paragraph,

2. work jointly to form simple sentences from a substitution table,

3. use think-pair-share to write simple sentences on describing school facilities from display of pictures,

4. practice copying paragraphs legibly and neatly,

5. compose a paragraph on the theme,

6. share their paragraphs with peers for review,

7. publish their best written paragraphs in a school or public magazine. 1.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. collaborate to conduct a research on the features of a well- developed paragraph,
2. work jointly to form simple sentences from a substitution table,
3. use think-pair-share to write simple sentences on describing school facilities from display of pictures,
4. practice copying paragraphs legibly and neatly,
5. compose a paragraph on the theme,
6. share their paragraphs with peers for review,
7. publish their best written paragraphs in a school or public magazine. 1.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Guided Writing: Paragraph Writing together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Critical thinking and problem solving: This is promoted as the learner explores views when conducting a research on the

features of a well-developed paragraph.

• Learning to learn: This is nurtured as the learner builds on their own learning experience by publishing their best written

paragraphs in a school or public magazine.

Values:
Integrity: This is promoted as the learner displays transparency by sharing their paragraphs with peers for review.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

Environmental awareness: This is promoted as the learner interacts with facilities within the school and identifies their

positions.

Link to Other Learning Areas:

The learner is able to relate the concept on composing paragraphs to their learning of writing in English.

APPENDIX 1: COMMUNITY SERVICE LEARNING PROJECT FOR UPPER PRIMARY LEVEL

INTRODUCTION

At this level, the goal of the CSL activity is to provide linkages between concepts learnt in the various Learning Activities and

the real life experiences. Learners begin to make connections between what they learn and the relevance to their daily life. CSL

is hosted in the Social studies learning area. The implementation of the CSL activity is a collaborative effort where the class

teacher coordinates and works with other subject teachers to design and implement the integrated CSL activity. Though they are

teacher-guided, the learners should progressively be given more autonomy to identify problems and come up with solutions. The

safety of the learners should also be taken into account when selecting the CSL activity. The following steps for the integrated

CSL activity should be staggered across the school terms:

Steps in carrying out the integrated CSL activity

1) Preparation


  -  Map out the targeted Core Competencies, values and specific learning areas skills for the CSL activity


  -  Identify resources required for the activity (locally available material
s) 
  -  Stagger the activities across the term (Set dates and time for the activitie
s) 
  -  Communicate to learners, parents/caregivers/guardians, school administration, teachers and other relevant stakeholders

in the school community


  -  Identify and develop assessment tools

74

2) Implementation CSL Activity


  -  Assigning roles to learners.


  -  Ensure every learner actively participates in the activity


  -  Observe learners as they carry out the CSL activity and record feedback.


  -  Use an appropriate assessment tool to assess both the process and the product (Assess learner’s work from the

beginning to the end produc
t) 
  -  Assess the targeted core competencies, values and subject skills.

3) Reflection on the CSL Activity

Conduct a self-evaluation session with learners on the integrated CSL activity undertaken by discussing the following:


  -  what went well and why


  -  what did not go well and why,


  -  what can be done differently next time


  -  what they have learnt.

There will be one integrated CSL activity that will be conducted annually. The thematic areas for the integrated CSL activity

will be derived from the broader categories of the PCIs and concepts from the various Learning Areas. Teachers are expected to

vary the themes yearly to allow learners to address different PCIs within their contexts. There should be a linkage between the

skills from the learning areas and the themes.

The integrated CSL activity will take a Whole School Approach (WS
A) where the entire school community is involved

(learners, parents/caregivers/guardians, school administration, teacher
s) . Parents/caregivers/guardians are key stakeholders in the

75

planning and execution of the CSL activity. Although the teacher takes the lead role in the planning and integration of the CSL

activity, learners will be expected to participate actively in the whole process.

The CSL activity provides an opportunity for the development of core competencies and the nurturing of various values. The

teacher is expected to vary the core competencies and values emphasised in the activity yearly.

Assessment of the CSL Activity

Assessment of the integrated CSL activity will focus on 3 components namely: skills from various learning areas applied in

carrying out the activity, and core competencies and values demonstrated. Assessment should focus on both the process and end

product of the CSL activity. The teacher will assess learners in groups using various tools such as an observation schedule,

checklist or rating scale or any other appropriate tool.

76
